definitions.explanation: A condition in which the arch of the foot is flattened so that the entire sole makes contact with the ground. Can cause discomfort when walking or running.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}から{扁平足|へんぺいそく}だった。
examples.english: I've had flat feet since childhood.

examples.japanese: {扁平足|へんぺいそく}だと{長時間|ちょうじかん}{歩|ある}くと{疲|つか}れやすい。
examples.english: With flat feet, you get tired easily when walking for a long time.

examples.japanese: {扁平足|へんぺいそく}を{改善|かいぜん}するためにインソールを{使|つか}い{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: I started using insoles to improve my flat feet.

notes:
Compound of {扁平|へんぺい} (flat; flattened) + {足|そく} (foot). A medical/anatomical term also used in everyday conversation about foot health and shoe fitting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {扁平足|へんぺいそく}の{矯正|きょうせい}: correction of flat feet
- {扁平足|へんぺいそく}{用|よう}インソール: insoles for flat feet
- {扁平足|へんぺいそく}の{人|ひと}: person with flat feet
- {扁平足|へんぺいそく}を{改善|かいぜん}する: to improve flat feet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {外反母趾|がいはんぼし}: bunion; hallux valgus — another common foot condition
- {土踏|つちふ}まず: arch of the foot — the part that is flattened in {扁平足|へんぺいそく}
- {偏平|へんぺい}: flat; flattened — the adjective form of the same kanji, sometimes written with this variant
